detailed_results.issue: I notice that people I assigned the test in October of 2025 have not received new tests. How long do the tests stay active in the system.
detailed_results.subject: Test Active in the system
detailed_results.expected_response:
Hi,


Tests in HackerRank remain active indefinitely unless a start and end time are set. 
Without these, tests do not expire automatically.



To set expiration times, specify a start and end date/time in the test settings. After expiration:

Invited candidates cannot access the test.
The "Invite" button is disabled; no new invitations can be sent.


To check or change expiration settings:

Go to the test's Settings and select the General section.
Update the Start date & time and End date & time fields as needed.
To keep the test active indefinitely, clear these fields by clicking the clear icon (X).


If the test has an expiration set, adjust these settings to enable new invitations.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
## Overview
Tests remain active only for the period you define in the **Expiry** settings. If no expiry is set, the invitation defaults to **Never** and the test stays active indefinitely.

## Prerequisites
- You must have permission to edit the test settings.

## Steps to view or change a test’s active period
1. Open the test in the **Screen** interface.
2. Click the **Expiry** dropdown in the test configuration panel.
3. Choose an expiry option (e.g., **1 day**, **1 week**, **Custom**).  
   - For **Custom**, select the exact end date, time, and time zone, then click **Save**.
4. The selected expiry date appears next to the dropdown.
5. Click **Save Changes** to apply the new expiration.

## Notes
- After the expiry time passes, the **Invite** button is disabled and no new candidates can be invited.
- You can also modify the start and end times under **Test expiration time** in the general settings.

## Reference
- [Modify Test Expiration Time](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/2979262079-modify-test-expiration-time)
- [Invite Candidates to a Test – Set an expiry date](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/6027855406-inviting-candidates-to-a-test)

detailed_results.issue:
I'm noticing that you all have many default versions of roles. (e.g. front end developer for react, angular, vue.js, etc.) What do you consider best practice 
for when to create a new test versus create a variant of the test? What are the advantages and disadvantages of using variants?
detailed_results.subject:
When should I create a variant versus
 have a different test?
detailed_results.expected_response:
Hi,


Consider these guidelines when choosing between creating a new test or a variant:



When to Use Test Variants:

Create variants to adapt a single test to different candidate profiles, 
such as roles with different tech stacks (React, Angular, Vue.js).
Variants streamline assessments by showing candidates only relevant sections and generating role-specific reports.


Advantages of Test Variants:

Reduces the need to manage multiple tests, improving efficiency.
Decreases maintenance while allowing scalable personalization.
Ensures candidates are tested on relevant content.


Disadvantages and Limitations of Test Variants:

A test must have at least two variants to function; you cannot delete a variant if only two exist.
Variants without logic are hidden from candidates until logic is added.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
## Overview
Test variants let you create multiple versions of a single test and serve the appropriate one based on a candidate’s input (e.g., tech stack, role). Use them when the core assessment is the same but you need to tailor questions, time limits, or instructions for different groups.

## Advantages
- **Reduced maintenance** – One test container instead of many separate tests.
- **Personalized experience** – Candidates only see sections relevant to their role/technology.
- **Clean reporting** – Results are tied to the specific variant, keeping analytics role‑specific.
- **Scalable** – Add new variants without duplicating the entire test.

## When to create a separate test
- The assessment content, objectives, or difficulty differ substantially.
- You need completely independent reporting or scoring models.
- Variants would become overly complex, making the test harder to manage.

## Disadvantages
The documentation does not list specific drawbacks of using variants. If a variant becomes too divergent from the base test, it may be simpler to create a distinct test.

## Best practice
- Start with a single test and add variants for each technology or role that shares the same core skill set.
- If the test logic, scoring, or overall structure diverges significantly, create a new test instead of a variant.

**Reference**: [Test Variants](/articles/3121307537-july-2025-release-notes) and [Create Test Variants](/articles/7530103378).
retrieved_context:
**Test Variants **

You can now create multiple variations of a test and deliver the correct one based on the candidate's input at login. This makes it easy to assess candidates working with different tech stacks—like Node.js, Python, or Java, using a single, streamlined test setup.

Candidates see only the sections relevant to them, and reports reflect just the variant they attempted, so insights stay clean, role-specific, and easy to evaluate. This reduces maintenance overhead while giving you the flexibility to personalize assessments at scale.

For more information, see [📄 Test Variants](/articles/7530103378).

Subtext for Test Variants

Candidates now see helpful subtext for each test variant, giving them more context about the available options and helping make informed decisions before they attempt the test.

For more information, see [📄 Create Test Variants](/articles/7530103378).

detailed_results.issue: I bought Visa Traveller's Cheques from Citicorp and they were stolen in Lisbon last night. What do I do?
detailed_results.expected_response:
Call the issuer (Citicorp) immediately. 
Freephone 1-800-645-6556 or collect 1-813-623-1709, Mon–Fri 6:30 am–2:30 pm EST. 

Automated cheque verification is available 24/7 in English/Spanish; outside Citicorp's hours your call is recorded and returned the next business day.

Have this info ready before you call, it's what the issuer will ask: cheque serial numbers, where and when you bought the cheques, how/when they were lost or stolen, and the issuer name (Citicorp). 

Refunds can typically be arranged within 24 hours, subject to T&Cs.
Notify the local police in Lisbon (Visa's safety guidance for lost/stolen cheques).
If you can't reach Citicorp, use Visa's traveller's-cheque contact form on visa.co.in.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
## Overview
You purchased Visa Traveller’s Cheques from Citicorp and they were stolen in Lisbon. You need to report the loss to the issuing bank and request a refund.

## Steps
1. **Contact the issuing bank immediately** – call Citicorp (use the number on your statement) or, if you cannot locate it, call Visa’s free‑phone line for traveller’s cheques [Document 4].
2. **Report the stolen cheques** – inform the bank that the cheques were stolen, providing the date, location (Lisbon) and any other relevant details.
3. **Request a refund** – the bank will ask for:
   - Cheque serial numbers
   - Purchase details (where and when you bought them)
   - Circumstances of the loss
   - Confirmation that Citicorp is the issuer
   (see the “Have your info ready” checklist) [Document 5].
4. **Await confirmation** – refunds are usually processed within 24 hours, subject to terms and conditions.

## Notes
- Keep any supporting documents (receipt, police report) handy in case the bank requests them.
- For general traveller’s cheque assistance, you can also visit Visa’s consumer support page [Document 2].

## Reference
- Visa Traveller’s Cheques – Consumer page: https://www.visa.co.in/support/consumer/travelers-cheques.html
- Suspect fraud – call issuing bank or freephone: https://www.visa.co.in/support/small-business/travelers-cheques.html
- Refund request details: https://www.visa.co.in/support/consumer/travelers-cheques.html
